newsitem.title: USA: Latin American companies favor Compaq PCs - survey.
newsitem.headline: Latin American companies favor Compaq PCs - survey.

text.p: By about three to two, Compaq Computer Corp personal computers are favored over International Business Machines Corp machines by executives buying information technology equipment for top Latin American corporations.
According to a survey of 722 large companies throughout Latin America by consultant firm International Data Corp, Compaq was the top vendor for more than 25 percent of the executives polled.

About 15 percent favored IBM machines, slightly more than those who preferred personal computers built by Acer Inc and Hewlett-Packard Co, International Data vice president Paul Pastrone told a technology marketing conference here. Machines made by Digital Equipment Corp and Dell Computer Corp were chosen as their favorite by fewer executives than those picking local brands.

Pastrone said the findings could be a boon for Compaq, since many leading Latin American companies are rethinking buying many different brands and considering purchasing all personal computers from single vendors.

Although accounting for only three percent of worldwide information technology expenditures, Latin America last year showed a 20.9 percent spending increase over 1995 while the worldwide sector growth rate was 13.1 percent in 1996.
